chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hammad, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Intermingle with the people to find out about them, and when you find out about them, (only then) travel/associate with them.

key_terms.تَخْبُرْهُمْ: To test / find out about them
key_terms.تَقْلِهِمْ: To travel / keep distance / separate from them

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim evaluate people before forming close relationships?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a pragmatic methodology for social interaction, emphasizing that active engagement ('mixing') is the necessary means to discern the true character ('knowing') of others. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'takhbur' (acquiring deep knowledge of people) as a prerequisite for wise companionship, reflecting the practical wisdom found in the sermons of Amir al-Mu'minin. It serves as a guide for navigating social dynamics with discernment rather than isolation.
